person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: depression and anxiety in the Chinese general population during the first weeks of COVID-19, and their association with how often people used social media
span.quote: A cross-sectional study among Chinese citizens aged≥18 years old was conducted during Jan 31 to Feb 2, 2020. Online survey was used to do rapid assessment.

span.label: how prevalent depression and anxiety were, and whether frequent social media exposure was associated with them after covariates
span.quote: After controlling for covariates, frequently SME was positively associated with high odds of anxiety (OR = 1.72, 95%CI: 1.31–2.26) and CDA (OR = 1.91, 95%CI: 1.52–2.41) compared with less SME.

span.label: prevalences with confidence intervals from established scales, and an adjusted association between social media exposure and anxiety
span.quote: The prevalence of depression, anxiety and combination of depression and anxiety (CDA) was 48.3% (95%CI: 46.9%-49.7%), 22.6% (95%CI: 21.4%-23.8%) and 19.4% (95%CI: 18.3%-20.6%) during COVID-19 outbroke in Wuhan, China.

span.label: existence
span.quote: The prevalence of depression, anxiety and combination of depression and anxiety (CDA) was 48.3% (95%CI: 46.9%-49.7%), 22.6% (95%CI: 21.4%-23.8%) and 19.4% (95%CI: 18.3%-20.6%) during COVID-19 outbroke in Wuhan, China.

span.label: population-scale depression and anxiety during a quarantine, co-occurring with near-universal social media use
span.quote: The prevalence of depression, anxiety and combination of depression and anxiety (CDA) was 48.3% (95%CI: 46.9%-49.7%), 22.6% (95%CI: 21.4%-23.8%) and 19.4% (95%CI: 18.3%-20.6%) during COVID-19 outbroke in Wuhan, China.

span.label: cross-sectional online survey of 4,872 adults across 31 provinces, WHO-5 for depression and GAD-7 for anxiety, multivariable logistic regression
span.term: cross-sectional online survey of 4,872 adults across 31 provinces, WHO-5 for depression and GAD-7 for anxiety, multivariable logistic regression
span.quote: Anxiety was assessed by Chinese version of generalized anxiety disorder scale (GAD-7)[ 15 , 16 ], which consists 7 symptoms. Participants were asked how often they were bothered by each symptom during the last 2 weeks. Response options were “not at all,” “several days,” “more than half the days,” and “nearly every day,” scored as 0, 1, 2, and 3, respectively.

span.label: the proposed pathway is exposure to information rather than to the virus: frequent social media exposure carries higher odds of anxiety (OR 1.72) and of combined depression-and-anxiety (OR 1.91) after covariates
span.quote: After controlling for covariates, frequently SME was positively associated with high odds of anxiety (OR = 1.72, 95%CI: 1.31–2.26) and CDA (OR = 1.91, 95%CI: 1.52–2.41) compared with less SME.

span.label: THE DEPRESSION SCALE IS A WELL-BEING SCALE, AND THE PAPER SAYS SO IN THE SAME PARAGRAPH: WHO-5's five items `REFLECT THE PRESENCE OR ABSENCE OF WELL-BEING RATHER THAN DEPRESSIVE SYMPTOMATOLOGY`, and a summed score below 13 `indicates depression`. 48.3% DEPRESSION IS 48.3% SCORING LOW ON WELL-BEING
span.quote: Depression was assessed by The Chinese version of WHO-Five Well-Being Index (WHO-5)[ 14 ], which consists of five positively worded items that reflect the presence or absence of well-being rather than depressive symptomatology.

span.label: the design cannot support the direction of the association: `it is difficult to accurately elucidate CAUSAL RELATIONSHIPS between SME and mental health`, with longitudinal designs named as what would
span.quote: First, this is a cross-sectional study, so it is difficult to accurately elucidate causal relationships between SME and mental health. Additional longitudinal studies, such as cohort studies or nested case-control studies, are essential in the future.

span.label: the sample is online and its skew is named with its direction - `some respondent bias, such as FEW ELDER CITIZENS' PARTICIPATION, may have affected the results`
span.quote: Although large sample, the survey was conducted online, which is suitable for rapid assessment, so some respondent bias, such as few elder citizens’ participation, may have affected the results.

span.label: and the adjustment is not claimed to be complete: `we CANNOT EXCLUDE the possibility of some residual confounding caused by unmeasured factors`
span.quote: Finally, although we did control for many covariates, we cannot exclude the possibility of some residual confounding caused by unmeasured factors.

span.label: the association is estimated AFTER controlling for demographic covariates, and the adjusted odds ratios are reported with intervals rather than raw proportions
span.note: eliminates: an association that is really an age or education difference between frequent and infrequent social media users · outcome: held
span.quote: After controlling for covariates, frequently SME was positively associated with high odds of anxiety (OR = 1.72, 95%CI: 1.31–2.26) and CDA (OR = 1.91, 95%CI: 1.52–2.41) compared with less SME.

span.label: whether the direction of the association can be established
span.note: eliminates: nothing - the design is cross-sectional and the paper says causal relationships are difficult to elucidate from it, naming cohort and nested case-control as what would be needed · outcome: failed
span.quote: First, this is a cross-sectional study, so it is difficult to accurately elucidate causal relationships between SME and mental health. Additional longitudinal studies, such as cohort studies or nested case-control studies, are essential in the future.

span.label: whether covariate adjustment removed the confounding
span.note: eliminates: nothing beyond what was measured - `we cannot exclude the possibility of some residual confounding caused by unmeasured factors` · outcome: failed
span.quote: Finally, although we did control for many covariates, we cannot exclude the possibility of some residual confounding caused by unmeasured factors.

span.label: whether the online sample represents the population the prevalence is quoted for
span.note: eliminates: nothing, and the direction is named: few elder citizens participated · outcome: failed
span.quote: Although large sample, the survey was conducted online, which is suitable for rapid assessment, so some respondent bias, such as few elder citizens’ participation, may have affected the results.

THE RESULT IS NAMED FOR A CONSTRUCT THE SCALE SAYS IT DOES NOT MEASURE, and the substitution is declared rather than hidden

span.label: anxiety, AS MEASURED HERE - GAD-7 at 10 or above, described as `A REASONABLE CUT POINT` and carrying two citations. The hedge and the citation are what qiu2020's cut-offs lack, and the difference is the whole comparison between the two records
span.quote: A score of 10 or greater represents a reasonable cut point for identifying cases of anxiety

span.label: social media exposure - a self-reported FREQUENCY, and the exposure variable in a cross-sectional design. `Frequently exposed` people are more anxious; whether the exposure or the anxiety came first is what the paper says it cannot tell
span.quote: First, this is a cross-sectional study, so it is difficult to accurately elucidate causal relationships between SME and mental health. Additional longitudinal studies, such as cohort studies or nested case-control studies, are essential in the future.

span.label: critiques → unmoderated social media during a public health emergency - the paper's `infodemic` recommendation follows directly from the association it measures
span.quote: The next implication is to combat with “infodemic” by monitoring and filtering out false information and promoting accurate information though cross-section collaborations.
